elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 3.2 retains automatic renewal ("will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term") and no mutual-written-agreement renewal was inserted; because the conditional automatic-renewal elements (30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder, 12-month cap) are not all met, this gateway element fails.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Renewal term is defined only by reference — "an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment" — and the initial Service Option Attachment/Order Form durations are not in the cited text; a term exceeding 12 months would create a multi-year auto-renewal. The edit does not fix the renewal term at 12 months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause requires "at least sixty (60) days' written notice prior to the end of the then-current term"; 60 days exceeds the preferred 30-day opt-out.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears in the rendered language; the reminder is only mentioned aspirationally in the margin comment ("our preferred position is a 30-day opt-out with a Vendor renewal reminder"), which is not operative.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the cited charging provision states "Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms" and contains no renewal uplift or escalation mechanic, so no capped-increase language is required.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 3.2: "unless either party gives the other party at least sixty (60) days' written notice prior to the end of the then-current term" — window is exactly 60 days, at the fallback ceiling, and is anchored to the end of the then-current term.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewal is "for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term" with no uplift language, and Charges are fixed by the Service Option Attachments and Order Forms; nothing in the cited text authorises a renewal price increase.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the 90-day non-renewal window is reduced to sixty (60) days measured to the end of the then-current term, and the price-cap element is vacuously satisfied because no renewal uplift mechanic exists in the cited charging provision.

Preferred level fails on four elements: renewal remains automatic rather than by mutual written agreement, the opt-out is 60 rather than 30 days, no Vendor reminder obligation was inserted, and the renewal term is still defined as equal to the previous term rather than capped at 12 months.

Minimality defect: the only change required to reach the fallback was replacing "ninety (90)" with "sixty (60)". The drafter also paraphrased untargeted words — original "notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior" became "gives the other party at least sixty (60) days' written notice prior". Restore the original verb construction and change only the numeral: "...unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term...".

Intent is preserved: the notice right remains mutual, the trigger remains the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment, the automatic-renewal structure and the Charges provisions are untouched, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Residual risk worth raising in negotiation (not a fallback defect): because each renewal term equals the previous term, any Service Option Attachment or Order Form with a term longer than 12 months produces an automatic multi-year renewal, which is walk-away territory under this rule; consider adding "provided that no renewal term will exceed twelve (12) months" if any attachment has a multi-year initial term.
